$description: Measured drift counts for the PACKAGE, read when the gate runs with --scope package. The monorepo's numbers are in baseline.json and are not comparable: this repo has an application binding the tokens, the package has demo chrome and fixtures, so H1 is properly larger here and the S-counts properly smaller. Judging the package against the app's numbers would fail it for being itself. X1's rule applies to each file independently — a number only moves down, in the change that earned it, with that run in runs.log.
$measured_by: node tokens/extract.mjs --out <dir> --verify, then node tokens/check.mjs --scope package in the extracted tree
$H1_because: 94 of the system tokens have no consumer inside the package, because the surfaces that consume them are the application and the application does not travel. It was 116 until components/ame/chrome.css shipped, which gave 22 of them their first consumer here: the .port-glass* rules bind tokens that previously had no reader in this tree. Ratcheted in the change that earned it, which is the only direction X1 permits. Fell 94 -> 92 on 2026-08-27 when nav.tsx stopped restating component.nav.pad and component.nav.item-height as JS strings and bound them instead: the two tokens were counted clientless BECAUSE the component had copied their values, so H1 was measuring the duplication.
